# Add Text to Image

- Route: `/tools/add-text-to-image`
- Kind: `tool`
- Category: `image`
- Slug: `add-text-to-image`

## Summary

Put a caption, title or watermark on a photo: choose the font, size, colour, outline and position, and download. (Image tools)

## Details

A caption on a screenshot, a title on a thumbnail, a copyright line in the corner of a photo: adding text is the most common image edit after cropping. Media Manipulator renders text onto an image on our servers with ImageMagick, with font, size, fill and outline colour, and a position chosen from nine anchors or exact pixel coordinates, and exports in the same or a different format.
### What it does
- Renders one block of text at any size with fill and outline colours.
- Six bundled fonts (sans, serif, mono in two families).
- Nine anchor positions or exact x/y placement.
- Combine with resize, crop, filters and metadata options in the same pass.
### How to use it
1. Upload an image: JPG, PNG, WebP, HEIC and more.
2. Type and style the text: Size, colours, outline, font, position.
3. Convert: ImageMagick draws the text.
4. Download: Save the captioned image.
### Supported formats
- Input: jpg, png, webp, gif, avif, heic, bmp, tiff
- Output: jpg, png, webp, avif, gif
### Technical details
- Text is rasterised at the output size; set the size in pixels relative to the image width.
- An outline of 2 to 4 px in a contrasting colour keeps text readable on busy photos.
- Choose PNG output to keep a transparent background for a watermark template.
### Use cases
- Caption a screenshot: Label what the viewer is looking at.
- Watermark a photo: Your name in the bottom corner.
- Thumbnail title: Big bold text for a video thumbnail.
- Meme: Top text, bottom text.
### FAQ
Q: Can I add more than one line?
A: One text block per pass; a line break in the text renders on a new line. Run the tool again for a second block.
Q: Can I use my own font?
A: Six bundled fonts are available; custom font upload is not supported.
Q: How do I place text exactly?
A: Pick an anchor and add x/y offsets in pixels.
Q: Will it reduce quality?
A: The image is re-encoded; choose PNG or a high JPG quality to keep it sharp.
